title: A2 Writing Quiz 5 — Home Life, Chores & Hobbies

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have already cleaned the kitchen.
I have already clean the kitchen.
I already have cleaned the kitchen yet.
I have cleaned already the kitchen.
questions.explanation: 'Already' usually comes between the auxiliary and past participle: 'have already cleaned'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have washed the dishes an hour ago.
I washed the dishes an hour ago.
I have wash the dishes an hour ago.
I am washing the dishes an hour ago.
questions.explanation: A specific past time ('an hour ago') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
I cooked dinner when the phone was ringing.
I was cook dinner when the phone rang.
I cooking was dinner when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This armchair is comfortabler than that one.
This armchair is more comfortable than that one.
This armchair is most comfortable than that one.
This armchair is comfortable than that one.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'more' for comparatives: 'more comfortable than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Painting is the most relaxing hobby for me.
Painting is the more relaxing hobby for me.
Painting is relaxingest hobby for me.
Painting is most relaxing hobby for me.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'the most' for superlatives: 'the most relaxing hobby'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: When I was a child, I could paint really well.
When I was a child, I could painted really well.
When I was a child, I can paint really well.
When I was a child, I could to paint really well.
questions.explanation: 'Could' + base verb expresses past ability: 'I could paint really well.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You should tidy your room before guests arrive.
You should to tidy your room before guests arrive.
You should tidying your room before guests arrive.
You should tidies your room before guests arrive.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'should tidy'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Would you like joining our book club?
Would you like to join our book club?
Would you like join our book club?
Would you liked to join our book club?
questions.explanation: 'Would like' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'would like to join'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'm going to repaint the living room this weekend.
I'm going repaint the living room this weekend.
I going to repaint the living room this weekend.
I'm going to repainting the living room this weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to repaint'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I finish my chores early, I will read a book.
If I finish my chores early, I read will a book.
If I will finish my chores early, I will read a book.
If I finished my chores early, I will read a book.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If I finish..., I will read...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She loves knitting scarves in winter.
She loves to knitting scarves in winter.
She loves knit scarves in winter.
She loves knitted scarves in winter.
questions.explanation: 'Love' can be followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'loves knitting'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We plan redecorating the bedroom next month.
We plan to redecorate the bedroom next month.
We plan redecorate the bedroom next month.
We plan for redecorate the bedroom next month.
questions.explanation: 'Plan' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'plan to redecorate'.

questions.question: We don't have ___ furniture in the new flat yet.
options: many
much
a lot
several
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negative sentences.

questions.question: I need ___ minutes to finish this puzzle.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Minutes' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'whereas'.
options: I enjoy reading, whereas my brother prefers gaming.
I enjoy reading, whereas but my brother prefers gaming.
Whereas I enjoy reading but my brother prefers gaming.
I enjoy reading whereas, my brother prefers gaming.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' shows a contrast between two clauses: 'I enjoy reading, whereas my brother prefers gaming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I won't finish the chores unless you help me.
I won't finish the chores unless you will help me.
I won't finish the chores unless don't you help me.
I won't finish the chores unless you helped me.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and is followed by present simple: 'unless you help me.'

questions.question: We are ___ milk, so I need to go shopping.
options: out of
off of
away of
short from
questions.explanation: 'Out of' means 'no longer having something': 'we are out of milk.'

questions.question: The bookshelf is ___ the window.
options: in front of
in the front
front of
at front of
questions.explanation: 'In front of' + noun describes a position: 'in front of the window.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I clean my room every Saturday.")
options: He said that he cleans his room every Saturday.
He said that he cleaned his room every Saturday.
He said that he was cleaning his room every Saturday.
He said he clean his room every Saturday.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple usually shifts to past simple: 'he cleaned his room every Saturday.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a neighbour asking to borrow a tool?
options: Dear Sir/Madam,
Hi Rashad,
To Whom It May Concern,
Dear Customer,
questions.explanation: 'Hi [Name],' is the natural, friendly greeting for a neighbour you know.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a friendly email asking a favour?
options: Yours faithfully,
Thanks a lot,
Sincerely,
Yours sincerely,
questions.explanation: 'Thanks a lot,' is a warm, informal closing suitable when asking a friend or neighbour for help.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Maybe we could rearrange the furniture this weekend.
Maybe we could to rearrange the furniture this weekend.
Maybe we could rearranging the furniture this weekend.
Maybe we can rearranged the furniture this weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Could' + base verb is used to make a gentle suggestion: 'we could rearrange...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the neighbour.' and 'The neighbour lent me a ladder.'?
options: This is the neighbour which lent me a ladder.
This is the neighbour who lent me a ladder.
This is the neighbour what lent me a ladder.
This is the neighbour lent me a ladder who.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in relative clauses: 'the neighbour who lent me a ladder.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I sometimes read before going to bed.
I read sometimes before going to bed.
Sometimes I read before going to bed always.
I read before sometimes going to bed.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'I sometimes read before going to bed.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know where I put my keys?
Do you know where did I put my keys?
Do you know where I put my keys.
Do you know, where I put my keys?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'where I put my keys?'

questions.question: My hands are tired because I ___ all morning.
options: paint
have painted
have been painting
painted
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action with duration: 'have been painting'.

questions.question: This toolbox isn't mine, it's ___.
options: we
our
ours
our's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's ours.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, dust the shelves. Then, vacuum the floor. Finally, open the windows.
First dust shelves then vacuum floor finally open windows.
Finally dust the shelves, first vacuum, then open windows.
Then first dust shelves, finally vacuum open windows.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Then,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Each of the rooms ___ a fresh coat of paint.
options: need
needs
needing
are needing
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'Each of the rooms needs...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You haven't finished the dishes yet, have you?
You haven't finished the dishes yet, haven't you?
You haven't finished the dishes yet, did you?
You haven't finished the dishes yet, have?
questions.explanation: Negative statement + positive tag: 'You haven't finished the dishes yet, have you?'
